lead.headline: 115,000 sign a petition to bring Jensen Huang back to Nvidia, Musk and Masad among them
lead.summary: The petition says signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees and 63,063 shareholders, with Elon Musk, Replit's Amjad Masad, Epic's Tim Sweeney and YC's Garry Tan named as supporters. It argues Huang was removed "without meaningful due process" and asks the board to reinstate him while an independent investigation runs. Huang resigned on Thursday; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and Nvidia's stock fell sharply through the week.

news.headline: Days before its IPO, Amodei calls compute Anthropic's "deepest business dilemma"
news.summary: Speaking with Jamie Dimon at a JPMorgan investor event on Friday, he said capacity has to be bought one to two years ahead, before anyone knows if revenue will justify it. Per Bloomberg, Anthropic has committed nearly $901B, mostly to compute and chips, with about $71B due by September 2027. The IPO is planned for 19 November.

news.headline: Anthropic: stop telling Claude Opus 5.5 to "think hard"
news.summary: Now the default on Pro, Max, Ultra and Team plans, Opus 5.5 reasons on its own, and Anthropic says responses without those phrases started faster with no measurable drop in quality. It recommends starting at Medium effort, which matched Opus 5 on High in its tests, and stating the goal, output and check-in points in one message.

news.headline: llama.cpp and ggml reach v1.0.0 and switch to semantic versioning
news.summary: After 3.5 years, major version bumps will now mark breaking changes to the public C API, so downstream tools can pin a release. v1.0.0 also removes 35 deprecated functions, adds FP8 KV caches and a MoE expert cache, hardens llama-server (SSRF, CORS, DNS rebinding) and adds a /v1/audio/speech endpoint. Released Friday.

news.headline: A Helsinki logician uses Claude to unlock Gödel's lost notebooks
news.summary: Jan von Plato, who leads a University of Helsinki project on 1,009 pages of Gödel's 1940s workbooks in obsolete Gabelsberger shorthand, had been moving at about a page a week. Given his transcriptions, Claude produced a 650-page digest in a couple of days, including a near-complete proof of the axiom of choice's independence that then passed Coq.

x_posts.name: Ethan Mollick
x_posts.text:
AI is getting better faster than our measurements are

I threw together SatBench, which measures how quickly major AI benchmarks become saturated (effectively beaten). Of 173 benchmarks cited by the Labs since 2023, 63% are now saturated. Saturation is happening faster each year. https://t.co/tITFRo7w0z
x_posts.why: A useful reminder to read launch-day benchmark tables with some caution.
